2) We expect a 35% spike in ingestion for our Q2 rollout; a frontloaded credit package helps but we also need a staged ramp so we don't over-commit early.

Ben — thanks for the clarifications. Quick responses below and a proposed path attached (proposed_term_sheet.xlsx):

- Co-term: we can align the contract to Nov 1 to match your fiscal year. That will create a short first partial period (Nov 1–Oct 31) for year 1; we propose pro-rating that period to avoid a big hit in year 1.
- Ramp cadence: Marissa, can you confirm a 3-step staged ramp (baseline, mid-roll, full) with quarterly true-ups and a 30% buffer for peak months? Ideally the buffer is covered by frontloaded accelerator credits and then reconciled after each quarter.
- Auto-renew: we can do a 1-year auto-renew by default but include an explicit 60-day opt-out window; for multi-year we can require an active renewal consent unless procurement accepts auto-renew terms.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Internal pricing call (Karthik + Sean) to finalize the laddered discount profile for a 3-year commit.
2) Marissa to produce a 1-page ramp cadence and onboarding milestones.
3) I will share a HubSpot deal link and a pre-filled DocuSign intent so procurement has paperwork to review.

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-457
DocuSign intent: https://www.docusign.com/intent/ACME-REN-457

Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Contract calendar merge + accelerator credits

Thanks Sean — read through the term sheet. A couple of recommended updates from pricing/legal perspective: 

- Co-term approach: prefer to co-term to Nov 1 but instead of pro-rating year 1 we can offer a short-term accelerator credit escrow that covers the difference between the pro-rate and an aligned minimum for QA months. That reduces billing noise at year boundary.
- Laddered pricing: suggest a stepped discount that increases in years 2 and 3 (2.5% / 5% incremental) tied to committed token bands.
- Canary ramp triggers: include a trigger clause where if usage exceeds the mid-roll projection by >40% for two consecutive months, we auto-approve a burst allocation for up to 60 days at a pre-agreed surge rate. Procurement needs visibility on surge unit pricing.

Marissa — can you draft the onboarding milestone table and sample invoice cadence (quarterly in arrears with true-up statement)?

Ben — please confirm whether the procurement team wants language that prohibits auto-renew for multi-year commitments (we can add or remove based on their appetite). If legal needs to redline, we can hand off to our contracts team (I propose we pre-position a short SOW that references the ramp milestones).

-Karthik
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
